blocks.prompt: 13. Find the \(8^{\text{th}}\) term from the end of the A.P. \(8, 11, 14, \ldots, 185\).
blocks.explanation:
The A.P. is finite: it starts at 8 and stops at 185.
We must find the 8th term counting backwards from 185.
Plan: read the list backwards; it is again an A.P., starting at 185 with common difference \(-3\).
steps:
Given: \(8, 11, 14, \ldots, 185\)
To find: the 8th term from the end.
Method: Reversed, the list is an A.P. with first term \(l = 185\) and common difference \(-d\). Its 8th term is \(l - 7d\).

Find the common difference
\[d = 11 - 8 = 3\]
Why: Neighbouring terms differ by 3.

Count back seven steps from the last term
\[\text{8th from end} = l - (8 - 1)d\]
\[= 185 - 7(3)\]
\[= 185 - 21 = 164\]
Why: The last term is the 1st from the end; seven steps back reach the 8th from the end.

Check by counting from the front
\[185 = 8 + (n - 1)3 \Rightarrow n = 60\]
\[\text{8th from end} = a_{60 - 8 + 1} = a_{53}\]
\[a_{53} = 8 + 52(3) = 164 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The \(k\)th term from the end of an \(n\)-term A.P. is the \((n - k + 1)\)th from the start.
blocks.final_answer: The \(8^{\text{th}}\) term from the end is \(164\).
